selected.look_here_first: Look for leaves divided into two rounded lobes by a central notch, pink-white orchidlike flowers, and flat legume pods.
Check the yellow-rayed flower heads and leafy basal growth, then examine the green disc florets and phyllaries to separate other Berlandiera species.
Look for an upright branched woody herb or shrub, alternate simple leaves, and small pale flowers crowded along narrow flowering spikes.
Check the rounded scalloped leaf blades on long petioles and small clustered flowers close to the ground; inspect where the petiole attaches.
Look underwater for rootless, branching stems with whorls of stiff, repeatedly forked narrow leaves, especially the bushy shoot tips.
Find the slender yellow-orange threadlike parasitic stems wrapped around a host plant, then examine tiny five-parted flowers and capsules for species ID.
Check numerous thin pinkish-white rays around yellow discs, hairy stems, and upper leaves that partly clasp the stem.
Look for narrow mostly untoothed leaves, stiff appressed stem hairs, and daisy heads with numerous fine white rays; compare the upper leaf bases.
Start at the flat creeping mat and opposite small leaves, often dark-blotched; examine milky sap, stem hairs and tiny cup-shaped cyathia.
Look for square aromatic stems, pairs of small opposite leaves, and small two-lipped flowers at nodes; inspect the flower calyx.
Check the compact barley-like terminal spike with long bristly awns, then inspect the three spikelets grouped at each rachis node.
